issues.description: StockIngredient constructor signature differs between artifacts. The problem statement (UML) declares a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int) (problem_statement.md), and the solution repository provides exactly that three-argument constructor (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java). The template repository instead only provides a four-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean strictValidation) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java). This mismatch will cause compilation errors or confusion when students (or example code in Main / SealSaloon) try to instantiate StockIngredient with three arguments as described in the task and shown in the solution. It therefore blocks straightforward implementation of acceptSupplyDelivery and other example usages.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template StockIngredient API match the problem statement and solution by providing the three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity). Add an overloaded three-argument constructor in the template that delegates to the existing four-argument constructor (for example: public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) { this(name, price, quantity, true); }) or replace the four-argument constructor with a three-argument version. This preserves pedagogical intent while preventing compilation errors when students instantiate StockIngredient with the three-argument signature.
